scope: Profile the current production solvers, identify removable work and rank next experiments. No solver or tuning changes; no new speedup claim.

method.cpu: Three complete-file captures per engine, alternating engine order by round; 24 workers plus the main isolate, 1000 us sampling interval. Report raw self samples, with each capture kept separate.
method.native: One complete-file single-worker V8 raw-tick capture per engine at 250 us, joined to native disassembly from that same process. Node source positions resolve inlined function origins; Wasm uses actual tick PCs, not CPU-profile function columns.
method.correctness: All eight captures matched complete expected stdout, with unchanged source hashes checked before and after each process. Every capture reported zero filesystem inputs.
limits: CPU percentages include main-isolate idle samples. They are sample shares, not independent elapsed-time components.
Single-worker native samples locate code regions; their percentages are not the 24-worker sample distribution.
PC sampling is imprecise. A sample on a comparison or instruction after a load does not establish cache latency, misprediction cost or that individual instruction's execution time.
Overlapping region counts must not be added. Removing work in a sampled block need not save its sample percentage.
Profiling durations are diagnostic only; no uninstrumented candidate benchmark was run in this pass.
Hardware counters are unavailable with the existing perf_event_paranoid=4. No system settings were changed.

nodeNative.finding: Both inlined lanes retain the dependent sequence predictor[id] -> records[stationId * 8 + 4] -> buffer[start + length], with bounds checks. Full key verification follows.

shortEquality.note: Half-open machine-offset ranges for station-head load through the equality branch, excluding the preceding bucket load. All 15 blocks have the verified five-instruction shape. Raw samples do not establish cache misses, branch mispredictions or expected savings.

rankedExperiments.name: Pack only predicted station ID and name length in the current 32768-entry predictor
rankedExperiments.evidence: The predictor and station-length source lines account for 21.2-21.6% of samples across all isolates in the three fresh captures. Native code confirms the dependent station-length load and bounds check in both lanes.
rankedExperiments.change: Use a Uint32Array with the existing 32768 entries and hash; carry the stored length directly into the existing equality helper. Preserve full-name and delimiter verification and the authoritative fallback.

historicalCounterevidence.result: 1.262 s candidate versus 1.234 s control; rejected.
historicalCounterevidence.difference: That experiment used 65536 32-bit entries (256 KiB), a different hash, and an equality helper that still reloaded records[r + 4]. The present helper accepts a validated length, so a 128 KiB packed table can actually remove that load.

historicalCounterevidence.result: 1.203 s candidate versus 1.167 s control; rejected.
historicalCounterevidence.difference: That predictor stored 16 bytes per entry (512 KiB), including key metadata. Do not repeat the large-record layout.

rankedExperiments.risk: The predictor still doubles from 64 to 128 KiB; removing one dependent load may lose to footprint and decoding costs. This is a controlled revisit, not an established win.
rankedExperiments.acceptance: First inspect native code to confirm both predicted-hit lanes lose the length load; then validate collisions/full tuples and benchmark fresh processes in matched alternating rounds.

rankedExperiments.name: Specialize the wide helper for its proven 16-31-byte name range
rankedExperiments.evidence: The only process_wide call is guarded by nonzero matches = bitmask(high == semicolon) << 16; ctz(matches) is therefore always 16..31. Native process_long nevertheless loads an all-ones low-vector mask, ANDs the low vector, and conditionally chooses the first hash for length < 16.
rankedExperiments.change: Express the 16..31 invariant directly, use the low vector unmasked, mask only the high vector with short_masks[length - 16], and always use the second hash. Remove the now-unused wide mask table if no references remain.
rankedExperiments.bounds: process_long receives 5.7-6.3% of 24-worker samples. In the single-worker capture, the two redundant instruction blocks receive just 60/13621 ticks (0.44%); this is a small target, not a predicted speedup.
rankedExperiments.risk: Code-layout changes and remaining lookup dependencies can outweigh the removed instructions. Preserve 32+ byte fallback, complete key equality and tail handling.
rankedExperiments.acceptance: Verify the native low-mask load/AND and hash-select instructions disappear, run boundary/collision correctness checks, then measure an end-to-end gain before retaining it.

rankedExperiments.name: Test earlier station-key loads across the existing three lanes
rankedExperiments.evidence: The 15 station-head-load/equality blocks collect 3976/9426 TurboFan parse_chunk ticks (42.18%, or 29.19% of all raw ticks). Each block follows a dependent bucket pointer load; current source finishes each lane lookup/update before the next.
rankedExperiments.change: Try issuing bucket addresses and key loads for the existing three lanes before consuming their equality results. Keep the same lane count, complete key verification and ordered updates when lanes resolve to the same station.

historicalCounterevidence.result: 1.039 s versus 1.026 s; rejected on the prior Core Ultra 7 258V kernel.
Preloading keys: 1.043 s versus 1.034 s; rejected on the prior machine/kernel.
XOR/zero-test equality: 0.492 s versus 0.481 s on this machine; native sequence grew from five to seven instructions.

rankedExperiments.risk: The profile establishes a hot region, not a cache-miss explanation. Older staging attempts lost; extra branches, live values and spills can erase any overlap. Lower confidence than the first two experiments.
rankedExperiments.acceptance: Inspect emitted load ordering and stack spills before benchmarking. Stop if the native scheduling is unchanged or the extra work dominates; retain only a repeatable full-file gain.

deprioritized: GC is only 0.37-0.66% of fresh samples, so allocation/GC tuning is not a leading target.
Node find is 1.1-1.3%; the predicted-hit path is a stronger target than generic collision probing.
Wasm read is 15.1-16.1% and Node read is 5.1-5.2%, but these are not pure disk-wait percentages. Prior chunk, asynchronous-reader and mmap experiments did not establish a repeatable gain.
Generic hot/likely hints previously left Wasm bytecode unchanged. Target the proven range invariant instead of another unmeasured attribute sweep.

The prior Node runtime-control timing gap remains unresolved. Earlier first-TurboFan timestamps do not quantify compiler CPU cost or establish a cause; a separate compilation trace is required before proposing a startup fix.
